source: NASA PDS Atmospheres Node — Mars 2020 MEDA bundle (calibrated + derived environmental data)
method: Mean of all samples in each 10-minute LMST bin (bin i covers minutes 10i to 10i+10 after local midnight); null = no sample. air_temp_c = mean of ATS_LOCAL_TEMP1-3 (mast booms, ~1.45 m) from CAL_ATS; pressure_pa = PRESSURE from DER_PS; relative_humidity_pct = LOCAL_RELATIVE_HUMIDITY from DER_RHS; ground_temp_c = GROUND_TEMP (TIRS brightness temperature) from CAL_TIRS; wind_ms = HORIZONTAL_WIND_SPEED from DER_WS (only exists up to sol 313). Ls and Mars year: Allison & McEwen (2000) / Mars24, mission sol 0 = local sol 52304.
caveats: MEDA data is released to the PDS in batches (about three times a year); this is not a live feed.
MEDA normally samples about 30 minutes of every hour, so many bins are null; clients interpolate across gaps.
Wind: derived wind ends on sol 313 at about 13:08 LMST (sensor damaged by wind-blown debris); there is no wind afterwards.
Perseverance crossed Jezero's rim in December 2024 (about sol 1355): recent curves are from the crater rim, not the crater floor or the delta.
No dust optical depth in these curves (MEDA RDS would need a radiative-transfer retrieval).

sources: Lemmon, M. T. (2026), Mastcam-Z Visible Aerosol Optical Depth Record v2, Mendeley Data, doi:10.17632/gktjp9jptb.2 (sol 311: tau 0.327 at 544 nm, preliminary)
Lemmon, M. T., et al. (2022), Dust, Sand, and Winds Within an Active Martian Storm in Jezero Crater, GRL 49, e2022GL100126, doi:10.1029/2022GL100126 (peak visible optical depth ~2)
